subject: Hosted→Dedicated migration: sizing validation and proposed cutover timeline for Acme Retail
messages:
From: Alex Porter <ops@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cope@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing for Dedicated migration and ETA

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our CTO asked for a concrete sizing & cutover plan so procurement can lock in the reserved capacity. We need to migrate from your Hosted API to a Dedicated pool for Q4 traffic. Key asks:
- Recommended GPU count / profiles for our sustained traffic (see attached sample CSV)
- Validation tests we should run during the dry-run window
- Expected downtime or risk window for cutover (we need a plan with fallbacks)
- Lead time for deployment and provisioning (vendor approvals + docs for our infra team)

Traffic snapshot attached. Typical model: 13B-chat with avg prompt+response tokens ~420; peak 95th-percentile concurrent requests ~380; avg requests/minute ~5200. We can provide more telemetry if needed.

Can you get us a proposal by early next week? Procurement needs an internal cost estimate.

Thanks,
Alex
Ops Lead, Acme Retail

[attachment: acme-traffic-sample.csv (csv)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cope@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Porter <ops@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated migration and ETA

Alex —

Appreciate the traffic snapshot, that helps a lot. Quick responses below and a plan for next steps:

1) Quick ask: can you confirm 95th pctl concurrency is measured at peak minute-level? If it's 95th across peak 5-minute windows that changes the tail behavior.

2) Sizing (ballpark, subject to verification):
   - Baseline: 8x A10G-equivalent slots for steady-state (~5000 rpm, avg 420 tokens, model 13B-chat).
   - Headroom/peaks: add autoscale pool that can burst to 18x slots for the 95th concurrency peaks.
   - KV/prefix cache: we'll enable per-customer cache to reduce repeated prefix work — expect ~12-18% token cost reduction during high-repeat flows.

3) Validation test plan:
   - Synthetic replay of your sample at 1.1x to validate tail latencies (we'll provide a JMeter harness).
   - Cold-start and checkpoint recovery tests (1 planned restart during dry-run window).
   - End-to-end integration test (API keys, VPC egress rules) with your infra team.

4) Timeline (high level):
   - Week 0: Sign dedicated contract + sizing sign-off (you).
   - Week 1–2: Provisioned pool creation and pre-deployment validation in our staging region.
   - Week 3: Dry-run with synthetic traffic & canary route (non-production cutover).
   - Week 4: Production cutover weekend (we recommend Sunday 02:00–04:00 local) with rollback option to Hosted for 30 minutes.

Costs and precise GPU SKU mapping depend on whether you want cost-optimized quantized variants — Rishi, should we propose both an MLP (quantized) and a float option?

I'll put together a sizing sheet and runbook. Looping Rishi for the proposal and finance/commit details.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0123

[attachment: acme-sizing-sheet.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cope@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Porter <ops@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Jun 2025 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated migration and ETA

Alex, Marissa —

Following up with a more concrete sizing validation after reviewing the sample:

Assumptions used: avg payload 420 tokens, average model throughput per A10G ~45 tokens/sec for the 13B-chat baseline (baseline kernels), 5% cache hit expected from your dataset.

Recommended committed config (conservative):
- Commit: 12 slots (A10G-equivalent) as reserved capacity; sustained handles ~6k rpm with p95 latency ~220ms.
- Burst pool: Autoscale up to 24 slots for peak windows (handles short spikes to 400+ concurrent).
- If you accept quantized int8 profile, we can reduce reserve to 9 slots sustained and burst to 18 slots (trade-off: 5–7% regen rate in edge cases).

Risk notes:
- Cutover should be scheduled during a low-traffic window and include a transparent fallback route to Hosted for 30–45 minutes.
- KV cache population: first 2 hours post-cutover will show higher token costs until hot prefixes populate.

Proposed testing checklist (we will deliver artifacts):
- Load replay harness + scripts (we will run with you and share results).
- Service-level smoke tests: API key validation, request/response schema checks, token-level accounting.
- Latency/throughput dashboard link to be enabled for your team.

Timeline tweak: if procurement needs vendor paperwork (PO + SOC attestation), add 1 week before Week 1. Dev, please confirm procurement lead time.

Regards,
Rishi
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cope@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Porter <ops@acmeretail.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Jun 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated migration and ETA

Alex —

Quick procurement note: our standard lead time for Dedicated contracts with reserved GPU commits is 10 business days for provisioning after signed PO + SOC docs. If Acme needs the cutover window earlier than the 4-week plan, we can expedite by pre-provisioning interim capacity but that requires a non-refundable 2-week provisioning deposit.

On the technical side, we will need a VPC peering/IP allowlist window scheduled with your infra on Week 2; Priya from CloudOps is copied for integration steps. Also attaching the migration runbook draft — this contains the rollback play and DNS cutover steps.

Thanks,
Dev
Director, Business Ops | Redwood Inference

[attachment: redwood-dedicated-runbook-v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Priya Shah <priya@cloudops.io>
To: Alex Porter <ops@acmeretail.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cope@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 14:19:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated migration and ETA

Hi team —

CloudOps will coordinate the peering and egress ACL changes. A few notes from our side:
- We'll need a 3-hour maintenance window with your infra to validate routes and NAT translations.
- Recommend smoke runs for token accounting during the maintenance (we can script this).
- For the dry-run canary, we'll use header-based routing to redirect 10% of traffic to Dedicated.

I'll attach the peering checklist and propose July 20 as the earliest maintenance window (pending your sign-off).

Cheers,
Priya
Senior Cloud Engineer, CloudOps Consulting

[attachment: cloudops-peering-checklist.md (md)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cope@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 02 Jul 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated migration and ETA

Team —

Thanks everyone. Alex, if Acme signs the commitment this week we can target:
- July 7: contract signed + PO received
- July 14–18: provision pool + staging validation (Week 1–2 accelerated)
- July 19: dry-run (10% canary) + smoke tests with CloudOps
- July 26: production cutover (Sunday, 02:00–04:00 local) with 45-minute fallback to Hosted route

I've attached the final runbook draft and a sizing tab that enumerates the two options (quantized vs float) with rough monthly unit economics. Rishi — let's finalize the pricing cadence and discount tiers in HubSpot and send a DocuSign. Dev — please confirm procurement lead time for the PO once Alex confirms.

Alex — please confirm the PO timeline and whether July 7 works for you. If procurement needs additional SOC docs, we'll share them immediately.

Best,
Marissa
